title: The Buried Ship
selection_exposition: Much later in the journey, the party returns to Nortune as Ft. Hurricane threatens Nisan.<New>Preparing the buried Fatima vessel forces Rico and Sigmund toward a private reckoning over Anne and the years of silence that followed.<Close>
blocks:
CHAPTER 4
THE BURIED SHIP<New>Nortune, before the battle with
Ft. Hurricane.<Close>

[A Fatima vessel sleeps beneath
Nortune. To release it, the party
must enter records sealed by
Committee B.]<Close>

ARCHIVE RECORD 1
SUBJECT: ANNE BANDERAS
STATUS: IMPERIAL HOUSEHOLD<New>ETHOS PRENATAL PROCEDURES
PURPOSE: FORCED EXPRESSION OF
DORMANT NONHUMAN TRAITS<Close>

<Rico>
They told her the treatment was
protecting me.<New>They were changing me before I was
even born.<Close>

ARCHIVE RECORD 2
ANNE AND INFANT REMOVED FROM PALACE
DURING SIGMUND'S AVEH INSPECTION<New>DEATH REPORTS: FABRICATED
IMPERIAL TOMB ENTRY: FABRICATED
DESTINATION: OUTER DISTRICT<Close>

<Fei>
The reports were made to survive
any ordinary investigation.<Close>

<Rico>
Paper, seals, witness statements...
They built a grave out of lies.<Close>

ARCHIVE RECORD 3
FAMILY SEAL RESPONSE CONFIRMED
SUBJECT: RICARDO BANDERAS<New>EXECUTIVE INQUIRY OPENED
COMMITTEE B SUPPRESSION APPROVED
SUBJECT RETURNED TO D BLOCK<Close>

<Bart>
That order came after the door
recognized you.<Close>

<Rico>
I know.<New>Now I want to hear him say it.<Close>

[Sigmund enters. For once, there
are no officers at his side.]<Close>

Sigmund
Can we speak in private?<Close>

[Rico looks first at Fei, then at
Bart. Bart starts to speak, but Fei
lightly catches his arm.]<New>[Rico holds their gaze, then gives
a slow nod. They leave. The door
closes behind them.]<Close>

[For several seconds neither man
speaks. Rico does not move farther
into the room.]<Close>

<Rico>
There. We're alone.<New>So say what you couldn't say in
front of them.<Close>

Sigmund
I have spent many years speaking as
the Kaiser of Kislev.<New>What I must tell you now cannot be
spoken from that office.<Close>

<Rico>
Then don't speak as the Kaiser.<Close>

Sigmund
Very well.<Close>

<Rico>
I want to know when.<New>Not when your men finished searching
old records. Not when it became safe
to admit it.<New>When did you first think I might be
your son?<Close>

Sigmund
The day you entered Anne's room.<Close>

<Rico>
When the door opened for me.<Close>

Sigmund
Yes. That lock was made to recognize
only Anne and me.<New>I saw the guard's report. I examined
the record left by the scanner.
There had been no malfunction.<Close>

<Rico>
But that is what you told everyone.<Close>

Sigmund
It is.<Close>

<Rico>
Before that day... you never knew I
was alive?<Close>

Sigmund
No. I knew Anne was carrying our
child when I left for the Aveh front.<New>While I was away, I was told the
child had died at birth.<Close>

Sigmund
A second dispatch came three days
later. It said Anne had died from a
fever brought on by the delivery.<Close>

<Rico>
And you believed it?<Close>

Sigmund
The reports bore the physician's
seal and the signatures of officers
who had served me for years.<New>They said disease had forced an
immediate cremation. There were
witnesses and a record of the ashes.<Close>

<Rico>
They gave you enough paper to bury
us without ever seeing a body.<Close>

Sigmund
Yes.<Close>

<Rico>
Did you go to the tomb when you
came back?<Close>

Sigmund
I did.<Close>

<Rico>
Did you open it?<Close>

Sigmund
No.<Close>

<Rico>
Why not?<Close>

Sigmund
Because I was grieving... and because
I wanted the report to be true.<Close>

<Rico>
You wanted your wife and child to
be dead?<Close>

Sigmund
I wanted to believe the men around
me had not taken them.<New>I returned to a government divided
between the army and the Ethos.<New>If the report was false, betrayal
had reached my own chambers.<Close>

<Rico>
So you stood in front of an urn and
called that proof.<Close>

Sigmund
I did. There is no honorable
explanation for it.<New>Only the truth of what I was willing
to accept.<Close>

<Rico>
Go on.<Close>

Sigmund
After you opened the door, I ordered
the old records from the sealed
archive.<New>I said I was investigating a defect.
In truth, I suspected what the door
had recognized.<Close>

<Rico>
How long did it take?<Close>

Sigmund
The first proof was found within two
days.<New>The physician on Anne's death report
had died before its written date.<Close>

Sigmund
The transport ledger showed Anne and
an infant removed from the palace.<New>Their names had been scraped away,
but the marks remained beneath the
ink.<Close>

<Rico>
An infant. Not a body.<Close>

Sigmund
Yes.<Close>

<Rico>
And the rest?<Close>

[Sigmund places a worn file on the
desk. He does not offer it to Rico.]<Close>

Sigmund
The Ethos kept another record. Anne
had been placed under their care
during her pregnancy.<New>The procedures were not treatment.
They sought to force your dormant
traits to appear.<Close>

<Rico>
Made into a demi-human.<Close>

Sigmund
That was their intention.<Close>

<Rico>
Did she know what they were doing?<Close>

Sigmund
Not at first. She believed the
procedures were protecting you.<New>When she questioned them, they kept
her sedated and cut her off from
everyone outside their order.<Close>

Sigmund
After your birth, she refused more
treatment. That was when they
removed both of you from the palace.<Close>

<Rico>
They didn't stop treating her.<Close>

Sigmund
No. The records show repeated
operations for years afterward.<New>They called them corrective. Each
one left her weaker.<Close>

[Beside Anne's file, the Memento
Pendant remains on Sigmund's desk.
Rico looks at it, then turns away.]<Close>

<Rico>
She used to cough until she couldn't
stand. Sometimes there was blood.<New>When I asked why the doctors never
made her better, she said medicine
took time.<Close>

<Rico>
She still defended them... even then.<Close>

Sigmund
Rico...<Close>

<Rico>
Don't. You weren't there.<Close>

Sigmund
No. I was not.<Close>

<Rico>
I stole food while she told me not
to. I carried water when she could
not lift the bucket.<New>When stones hit our window, she said
the people were afraid because they
did not understand.<Close>

<Rico>
She kept finding gentle words for
everyone who hurt us.<New>She even found them for you.<Close>

Sigmund
What did she tell you?<Close>

<Rico>
That my father was a great man. That
there had to be a reason he could
not come for us.<New>She said it so many times, I think
she was trying to make herself
believe it too.<Close>

Sigmund
The final medical entry says Anne
died ten years after you were born.<New>The Ethos physician wrote that the
subject was no longer useful.<Close>

<Rico>
Subject...<Close>

Sigmund
I had that man found.<Close>

<Rico>
Is he alive?<Close>

Sigmund
No. He died in Ethos custody before
I could question him.<Close>

<Rico>
Convenient.<Close>

Sigmund
Yes. Far too convenient.<Close>

<Rico>
You found all this after I opened
that door.<New>You knew the report was false. You
knew my mother had been taken. You
knew there was a living child.<Close>

Sigmund
Yes.<Close>

<Rico>
Then why did you hand me over to the
Battling Committee?<Close>

[Sigmund does not answer. Rico steps
closer.]<Close>

<Rico>
Don't tell me you needed more proof.
The door gave you enough to stop an
arrest.<New>You could have ordered the guards
out. You could have asked me one
question about her.<Close>

<Rico>
Instead, you called the lock broken
and sent me back to D Block. Why?<Close>

Sigmund
Because I was afraid.<Close>

<Rico>
Of the Committee?<Close>

Sigmund
Of what the truth would expose.<New>Kislev's officers were taught that
demi-humans were unfit to serve.
Families were driven from the city
under decrees bearing my seal.<Close>

Sigmund
The Committee was already claiming
you had tried to kill me.<New>If I acknowledged you, the army
would see a contradiction in the
house it served.<Close>

<Rico>
So you chose the government.<Close>

Sigmund
Yes.<Close>

<Rico>
Say the whole thing.<Close>

Sigmund
When you came through that door, I
knew enough to protect you, and I
chose not to do it.<New>I watched the guards take you away
because keeping my position seemed
more important.<Close>

Sigmund
Whatever had been done before that
day... that choice was mine.<New>I abandoned you, Rico.<Close>

[Rico's fist rises. For an instant,
it seems he will strike Sigmund.<New>Instead he plants it against the
desk. The wood groans.]<Close>

<Rico>
I spent half my life hating a man
who never came.<New>I thought the reason would make it
simple. Maybe you would be a monster.
Then I could hate you and be done.<Close>

<Rico>
But you were a man in this room,
reading reports, making one choice
after another.<New>That is worse in a different way.<Close>

Sigmund
I know.<Close>

<Rico>
No. You know what is written in that
file.<New>I know what those choices felt like
outside this palace.<Close>

Sigmund
Then tell me.<Close>

<Rico>
They felt like shop doors closing
when Mother came near.<New>Like soldiers checking my hands and
teeth before letting me cross a
street.<Close>

<Rico>
They felt like D Block, where men
could be caged, drugged and made to
fight because people above them had
decided they counted for less.<Close>

Sigmund
The first decrees were issued while
I was at the front. The Ethos used
my seal without my knowledge.<Close>

<Rico>
And when you returned?<Close>

Sigmund
I left them in force.<Close>

<Rico>
Why?<Close>

Sigmund
The capital was close to revolt. The
Ethos taught humans to blame
demi-humans for shortage and defeat.<New>I said I would remove the decrees
when Kislev was secure.<Close>

<Rico>
But Kislev is never secure, is it?
There is always Aveh, Gebler, or
somebody inside your government.<New>So the right time never came.<Close>

Sigmund
No. It did not.<Close>

<Rico>
Then after a while, they weren't the
Ethos' laws anymore.<New>They were yours.<Close>

Sigmund
Yes.<Close>

<Rico>
What about Committee B? You drove
most of the Ethos out.<New>Why leave them in charge of the
Battling system?<Close>

Sigmund
Because it supplied pilots, machines
and revenue. It kept those most
likely to resist inside D Block.<New>I thought I could use what remained
of the Ethos without restoring their
power.<Close>

<Rico>
They used you too.<New>They put their crimes under an
Imperial code and made the Kaiser
responsible for enforcing it.<Close>

Sigmund
That is true.<Close>

<Rico>
They called me an assassin and
arranged a public execution.<New>You knew they were lying.<Close>

Sigmund
I knew their evidence was false. I
ordered a private inquiry, but did
not revoke the sentence openly.<New>Gebler was moving against the city.
I said the struggle could wait.<Close>

<Rico>
Everything waited except the
execution.<Close>

Sigmund
Yes.<Close>

[A long silence. Machinery inside
the wall gives a low, steady hum.]<Close>

Sigmund
I cannot return what was taken. I
cannot ask Anne to forgive me.<New>I have no right to demand forgiveness
from you. But if there is something
I can still do, tell me.<Close>

<Rico>
You really don't know?<Close>

Sigmund
I know what I intend to do. I am
asking what you require of me.<Close>

<Rico>
Then listen. I don't want a room in
this palace. I don't want a title.<New>And I don't want an heir announced
so ministers can call this a family
quarrel.<Close>

Sigmund
What do you want announced?<Close>

<Rico>
The truth. All of it.<New>Tell Kislev what was done to Anne.
Tell them our deaths were forged.<Close>

<Rico>
Tell them the anti-demi-human decrees
were kept because they were useful.<New>And tell them that when you learned
I was alive, you let the Committee
take me anyway.<Close>

Sigmund
Several senior officers will be
implicated. Some command units that
protect the capital.<New>Committee B will move before an
inquiry can begin.<Close>

<Rico>
Then don't call it an inquiry and
give them time to hide everything.<New>Remove their authority. Open their
prisons. Take the records before
they can burn them.<Close>

Sigmund
Battling cannot be ended by one
order. Thousands in D Block depend
on its ration allotments.<New>If I simply close the arena, the
prisoners will be first to starve.<Close>

<Rico>
Keep the food moving and end the
contracts that make prisoners kill
for it.<New>Put supplies under the civil district.
Let Battlers choose the army, paid
work, or freedom.<Close>

Sigmund
And the decrees?<Close>

<Rico>
Repeal them. Not next month. Not
after another committee studies them.<New>Give demi-humans the same right to
live, work, serve, and bring charges
against human officers.<Close>

<Rico>
Then review every sentence under
Code B.<New>Some people have been in D Block so
long, nobody remembers what they
were accused of.<Close>

Sigmund
That review will reveal crimes by the
state on a scale that cannot be
concealed.<Close>

<Rico>
That is the point.<Close>

Sigmund
There may be riots. Men who obeyed
those laws all their lives will not
accept that they were unjust.<Close>

<Rico>
Of course they won't. You spent years
teaching them who to despise.<New>One speech won't change that. But the
law can stop helping them do it.<Close>

<Rico>
After that, you keep speaking and
enforcing it, even when the people
cheering today call you a traitor
tomorrow.<Close>

Sigmund
You ask me to place Kislev above the
throne.<Close>

<Rico>
I'm asking you to decide what Kislev
is.<New>If it is only the throne, army, and
people the Ethos called human, then
Mother and I were never part of it.<Close>

<Rico>
Neither were the people who kept
your factories running and Gears
standing.<New>If Kislev means all of them, prove
it while you have the power.<Close>

Sigmund
When I drove the Ethos from council,
I thought resolve meant never
yielding.<New>I treated every compromise as a
burden I could carry until victory.<Close>

<Rico>
Burdens don't stay on the man who
chooses them.<New>They fall on everybody underneath
him.<Close>

Sigmund
Yes. I see that now.<Close>

<Rico>
Seeing it is not enough.<Close>

Sigmund
No. It is not.<Close>

[Sigmund crosses to the communication
panel, then pauses above the switch.]<Close>

Sigmund
At dawn I will convene the civil
council and every district commander.<New>Committee B's archives will be seized
before the summons is announced.<Close>

Sigmund
I will suspend Code B, place repeal
before the council, and release
Anne's records with my testimony.<Close>

<Rico>
Your ministers will cut out the
parts that make you look guilty.<Close>

Sigmund
Then there will be no prepared
statement for them to alter.<Close>

<Rico>
And the prisoners?<Close>

Sigmund
No execution, transfer, or forced
contract may proceed under Code B.<New>The review will include people chosen
by the Battlers and demi-human
districts, not only my officers.<Close>

[Rico studies him, searching his
face for hesitation.]<Close>

<Rico>
You have thought about this before.<Close>

Sigmund
Every night since the file was
completed.<Close>

<Rico>
But you did nothing.<Close>

Sigmund
I waited for a way to act without
endangering the country.<New>There is no such way. That was one
more truth I used delay to avoid.<Close>

<Rico>
Then stop waiting.<Close>
[Sigmund presses the switch.]<Close>

Sigmund
This is Sigmund. Place the palace
guard under direct command.<New>Seal the offices of Committee B. No
record is to be removed or destroyed.<Close>

Sigmund
Summon the civil council and all
district commanders for dawn.<New>I will address Kislev in open session.<Close>

ADJUTANT
Kaiser...? On what matter?<Close>
[Sigmund looks at Rico.]<Close>

Sigmund
On crimes committed under the
authority of this government...
including my own.<Close>

ADJUTANT
Yes, Kaiser.<Close>

[The channel closes. Sigmund removes
the Imperial signet and sets it beside
Anne's file.]<Close>

Sigmund
Will you be present?<Close>

<Rico>
If you want them to see a father and
son reunited, no.<Close>

Sigmund
That is not what I am asking.<Close>

<Rico>
Then why?<Close>

Sigmund
The council has heard my voice for
years. They should look upon someone
who lived beneath those laws.<New>And if I soften the truth, I want
you there to stop me.<Close>

<Rico>
I'll be there. Not as your heir. Not
as a symbol beside the throne.<New>I'll stand as the man your government
called a mutant and condemned under
Code B.<Close>

<Rico>
What happens after that depends on
what you do.<Close>

Sigmund
I understand.<Close>

<Rico>
No promises about us. You don't get
to settle that tonight.<New>And don't ask me to call you Father.<Close>

Sigmund
I will not.<Close>

[Sigmund holds out Anne's file.
Rico looks at it for a long time
before taking it.]<Close>

Sigmund
These records belong with you.<Close>

<Rico>
They belong in the public archive
when the copies are made.<New>After that... I'll decide what
belongs with me.<Close>

Sigmund
Very well.<Close>

[Rico turns toward the door, then
stops.]<Close>

<Rico>
Mother waited for you until she
couldn't wait anymore. I won't.<New>If you lose your nerve tomorrow,
I will tell Kislev myself.<Close>

Sigmund
Then I must make certain you have
no need to.<Close>

[Rico opens the door. Fei and Bart
wait in the corridor.<New>Rico steps out carrying Anne's file.
Behind him, Sigmund remains beside
the desk without his signet.]<Close>

[An alarm interrupts the silence.
Committee B has begun B Protocol.]<Close>
CHAPTER 4 COMPLETE<Close>
